items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-04: "Gate it now")
items.title: The loss reflex's recipe rescue retools to power only on a grid that is short
items.design: Found by BL-1485 (power grid measure), 2026-11-04: 59 of 60 play-built power plants by t50 are not builds but the loss reflex's cross-group recipe rescue (economy_system.cpp, 'Recipe rescue'): a floored steel plant retools to power because power's price/base beats a floored output, on grids the measure reads as not short (55 of 59; mean power price 0.75 of base; seed 37: draw 143.7 vs output 738, six steel plants switch in one tick). RULED (Ben, 2026-11-04): gate the rescue now on the same grid measure (body_power_grid_gap, own buildings live, others nominal), for every nation including the player's - the rescue is a mechanical reflex, not a strategic act. A rescue onto power is refused unless the target grid is short. Check: market_viability full tier (G1t50 >= 84, power plants decommissioned at t50 and the PW line against the BL-1485 reading), world_determinism, building_upkeep. MEASURED 2026-11-04 (Lane W): the gate cut play-built power plants 71 -> 15 (none decommissioned) but G1t50 fell to 83.6 (floor 84): the steel plants it no longer rescues stay idle. Parked on branch bl1492-rescue-grid-gate-g1t50-fail (7316da4e). RULED (Ben, 2026-11-04): rescue elsewhere - a refused power rescue tries the next-best non-power recipe before idling; then re-gate. The loss reflex keeps skipping the player's nation (Ben, 2026-11-04: keep the skip), so the gate binds rivals only. RULING (Ben, 2026-11-05): keep parked. Rescue elsewhere on bl1492-rescue-elsewhere (79ff0984) cuts play-built power 71 -> 15 but G1t50 83.6 < 84: floored steel plants refused a power retool idle. Revisit with seed re-curation (BL-1413).

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-05: sprint 64 naval design form)
items.title: Measure how much trade crosses water, per seed and per nation, before any raid number is set
items.design: MEASURE FIRST. Raiding and blockade are worth only what crosses the water. Per library seed and per major: the share of landed cargo value on a sea leg, the same for a nation's imports, and how many ports carry it. Goldens cannot see trade, so this is a harness reading on the shipped start. If the share is small, that is a finding to raise with Ben before patrol, escort and raid are tuned. Run after sprint 63's economy wave. Patrol, escort and raid were built ahead of this reading, on a first-cut raid_take_permille_per_day of 100: in the harness field one raider takes about 97% of whole crossings. Read that against real lanes here and tune in BL-1535 (naval war reading). READING (2026-11-10 naval_reading, sixteen library seeds, 40 ticks, after the re-bless (f48be3f6)): Sea legs carry 58.7% of landed cargo value pooled (17.5% seed 22 to 96.3% seed 7); per major, median 82% of imports and 82% of exports by value go by sea (n=54 / 45; 3 and 2 majors under 10%); 7 to 31 ports carry it a seed. The share is large, so the premise holds and nothing is raised; the harness is tools/verify/naval_reading.cpp.

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-09)
main session (Ben, 2026-11-05: sprint 64 naval design form)
items.title: Close the sprint on a measured war at sea and the one re-bless
items.design: v0.3.0 needs the naval system and a playtest with a few wars. Sweep the library: fleets raised, raids landed, ports closed, landings made, treasuries under fleet upkeep. Then the sprint's one re-bless, described by rebless_shape_probe, ruling-check, and a live war played to a landing. It also owes the one reading the blockade could not show on a fixture: a clearing price moving at a blockaded market on a real seed. It also owes a landed army on a real seed: its stocks running down with no port, and holding once it takes one. PROGRESS 2026-11-10: the re-bless is taken (f48be3f6, 16/16). Library sweep (2026-11-10 naval_reading, sixteen library seeds, 40 ticks, after the re-bless (f48be3f6)): Raids material on two seeds only (seed 54 4.1% of sea value, seed 0 2.0%); a blockade ran on seeds 0, 31, 60, one port closed each; 5 units landed (seeds 31, 60), all at full LP share, so food held at 1000; 7 rival ship hires on 4 seeds; crew wages 42 to 210 a tick against fleet treasuries 21k to 286k. Blockade price: Blockaded price against its own price the tick before closing, netted of the other markets' move over the same span: seed 0 0.998 vs 1.040, seed 31 1.038 vs 1.038, seed 60 1.055 vs 1.026 (110, 864, 880 readings). The blockaded markets read 14-24% below other markets, but they were cheap before closing. So the blockade does not move a clearing price on these seeds: NR-1156 (blockade price). Still owed: a staged landing with no port (none arose uncovered), ruling-check, a live war played to a landing. 2026-11-10: the blockade price is settled (Ben, NR-1156, "Accept as is"): a closure moves prices both ways, written in MILITARY.md § Blockade. naval_reading closure lines, seeds 31 and 60, 40 ticks, 2026-11-10: one port of 5 closed for 16 ticks; seed 31 landings -67%, steel demand 73 -> 21 (construction/upkeep/trade channel) against supply 27 -> 11, steel -20% against +8% elsewhere; seed 60 tobacco +88% against +53% elsewhere.

items.author: main session (naval_reading, 2026-11-10)
items.title: A price falls as its supply vanishes, with demand flat
items.design: MARKETS.md § Price resolution: target = base x sqrt(demand / supply), and base x ceil_mult with no supply, so a price should climb as supply falls toward zero. Read on seed 31 at the blockaded market 47921 (naval_reading, 40 ticks, 2026-11-10): machinery supply 1.7 -> 0.1 a tick, demand 7.5 flat (all background), yet the price fell 473.43 -> 370.00 while other markets moved x0.969. A price of 473 standing above what looks like the band ceiling (370) means a price is written outside resolve_price, or the ceiling moved. Find which, and whether it is a defect or a rule the doc does not state. Read before changing anything.
